clue.text: Trying places, maybe, for those involved with rackets

definitions.meaning: courts of law where cases are tried, read as courts that are hard going
tennis players wield rackets on firm surfaced courts

explanation.surface: A remark about criminals involved in rackets facing tough trials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rackets' suggests crime and 'trying places' suggests law courts; the second sense is tennis rackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is played on hard, clay or grass surfaces; a law court that tries a case could also be a difficult one.

clue.text: William or Mary, for what it's worth

definitions.text: William or Mary, for what it's worth

parts.words: William or Mary, for what it's worth
parts.note: William III and Mary II reigned jointly, so each was one of two monarchs; a coin of that name was worth ten shillings

explanation.surface: A remark on the value of one of a pair of joint monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: William and Mary shared the English throne from 1689; the gold coin of the same name was worth ten shillings, half a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Each co-ruler held a share of the crown, and the phrase also names an old British gold coin.

clue.text: Growth of Gibraltar originally?

parts.note: Gibraltar is known as the Rock, so something growing there is playfully a plant of the Rock

explanation.surface: A question about what first grew on Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar is nicknamed 'the Rock'; an alpine plant that grows among stones is named after rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine flowers grown in stony gardens are called by this name, and the Rock is Gibraltar's nickname.

clue.text: Character twice spotted in Panama

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark made of two dots one above the other
Colón is a port city in Panama at the Atlantic end of the canal

explanation.surface: Someone seen twice in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but it is a printed symbol with two spots.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark consists of two dots, and the port city at the canal's Caribbean entrance has the same name.

clue.text: Girl at the Hertfordshire town in the dark

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county just north of London

explanation.surface: A girl in a Hertfordshire town after nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark means knowing nothing about something, so ignorant of it.

clue.text: Mathematicians called Steptoe, perhaps

definitions.meaning: people who tot up figures, adding them
Albert and Harold Steptoe were rag-and-bone men in the BBC sitcom Steptoe and Son, a trade also called by this name

explanation.surface: Mathematicians who go by the surname Steptoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about scrap dealers who collected junk with a horse and cart.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot is to add up, and rag-and-bone collectors were known by the same word in British slang.

clue.text: She's crazy about you, we hear

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other here

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word you is replaced by a letter pronounced the same

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like you

explanation.surface: A woman who is mad about you.
explanation.definitionFit: Maud is a woman's name, as in Tennyson's poem.

clue.text: Excuse for a party one joins

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone joining a party as an excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere used as an excuse.

clue.text: How the nightwatchman kept himself amused off duty?

definitions.text: How the nightwatchman kept himself amused off duty?

parts.words: How the nightwatchman kept himself amused off duty?
parts.note: a night worker sleeps by day, so any dreams come in daytime; the word also means let the mind wander

explanation.surface: What a night guard did with his free time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working nights sleeps by day, so dreams then; the word means fantasised idly.

clue.text: Left with sufficient strength can be easily moved

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
able means having the power or strength to do something

explanation.surface: Something that can be shifted once enough force is applied.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase, 'can be easily moved', standing for an adjective meaning movable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily carried or moved about is light and mobile.

clue.text: Municipal body putting planner in his place?

definitions.text: Municipal body putting planner in his place?

parts.words: Municipal body putting planner in his place?
parts.note: a council employs planners in its area, and planning officers work for the council of their place

explanation.surface: A town council putting a planning officer in his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting someone in his place' suggests a rebuke; read literally, the council places planners in its neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A council governing a town or district is the municipal body that employs planning officers.

clue.text: See 10
Could nevertheless prove a close match

definitions.text: Could nevertheless prove a close match

parts.words: Could nevertheless prove a close match
parts.note: in chess, a game opening with king's pawn moves; the paradox is that something 'open' can still be close-fought

explanation.surface: A game that may yet turn out tight.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess an opening with 1 e4 e5 is classed by this name; 'close' plays against 'open'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess classifies openings as open or closed, and an open one may still be a tight contest.

clue.text: One who sets his sights on reaching a German town

definitions.text: One who sets his sights on reaching
definitions.meaning: someone who makes an attempt or effort
An ancient city on the Moselle in western Germany

explanation.surface: Someone aiming to reach a town in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries is a person making efforts, and the Moselle city is the oldest in Germany.

clue.text: See 1
By the sound of it look for a drink, but find a vegetable

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the phrase is spoken and heard as another spelling

parts.note: to look for is to seek, and a drink is ale

explanation.surface: Hoping for a beer but getting greens instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea kale is a coastal plant whose young shoots are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: They indict a couple of hundred employers

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them make CC
those who employ something use it, so they are users

explanation.surface: Two hundred bosses bringing charges.
explanation.definitionFit: People who indict others bring formal charges against them.

clue.text: Remote location from which Stalin henchman is heading back

indicators.note: heading back says the word is runs in the reverse direction

parts.note: Lavrenti Beria was Stalin's secret police chief

explanation.surface: A distant place from which a henchman of Stalin returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading back' turns IS into SI, which goes before BERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast frozen region of northern Asia is a byword for remoteness and exile.

clue.text: Untidy Hugh's backdoor entry in dirty boots?

indicators.note: entry means a group of letters is put into another word

parts.note: the word door read back to front

indicators.note: untidy says the letters of Hugh's are jumbled

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Messy Hugh comes in the back door in muddy boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untidy' rearranges HUGHS as UGHSH, and 'entry' puts it inside ROOD, which is DOOR backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Shod roughly, as with nailed horseshoes, suggests heavy dirty footwear trampling over things.

clue.text: Virginia, I can't possibly see in Rome

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of I can't could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Virginia complaining she can't make it to see Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ICANT as TICAN. 'See' is a bishop's seat, as in the Holy See.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy's seat, the Holy See, is in this enclave inside Rome.

clue.text: Falls and gets up again with artist's help

indicators.note: in a down clue gets up means the word again is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone tumbling and rising once more with a painter's assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls lie on the border between Canada and the US.

clue.text: Introduction to a notable work

definitions.meaning: an opening piece that comes before the main part
Wordsworth's long autobiographical poem has this title

explanation.surface: An introduction to an important piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening piece leads into the main work, and Wordsworth's long poem bears the name.

clue.text: Quietly shared out in a manner of speaking

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: shared out suggests the letters of shared are dealt round into a new order

explanation.surface: Something quietly divided up, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worded a certain way has been put in a particular manner of expression.

clue.text: Gives encouragement to sources of growth

definitions.meaning: to cheer on, as a fan does for a team
the underground parts through which plants draw nourishment

explanation.surface: Encouraging the beginnings of growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheering on a side is backing it, and plants grow from their underground parts.

clue.text: Where silver too can be unearthed in the Antipodes

indicators.note: unearthed suggests the letters are dug up and turned over into a new order

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A place down under where silver might be mined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be unearthed' rearranges AG and TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region in the south of New Zealand, part of the Antipodes, famed for its gold rush.

clue.text: Impenetrable and in a manner mean

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing
tight means stingy

explanation.surface: Someone who is unreachable and rather stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sealed so nothing gets through is impermeable.

clue.text: Exchanged Eire's currency in France

indicators.note: exchanged suggests the letters of Eire's are swapped about

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Irish money being changed into French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' is something with a current, a river; the Isère flows through south-east France.
explanation.definitionFit: A river carries a current, and this one is a tributary of the Rhône in France.

clue.text: Drop out in a dig

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of drop are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone dropping out in an excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: A poke or jab, whether with a finger or in words, is a dig.

clue.text: Not currently creditable due to some liability

definitions.text: Not currently creditable due to some liability

parts.words: Not currently creditable due to some liability
parts.note: someone behind with payments owes money, so for now is in the red

explanation.surface: Someone unbelievable at the moment owing to a weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creditable' suggests trustworthy, but it means in credit; a debt still owing puts you behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind on payments means owing money that is overdue.

clue.text: Sweetheart with the right air

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A lover with the right attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper sky or heavens were poetically called by this word, meaning the clear air.

clue.text: Time for reflection

indicators.note: for reflection says the word reads identically in a mirror, back to front

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A moment set aside for thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, twelve o'clock, is a time of day.

clue.text: To act so impetuously is anything but hair-raising

definitions.text: To act so impetuously is anything but hair-raising

parts.words: To act so impetuously is anything but hair-raising
parts.note: the idiom 'go at it ...' means rush in recklessly, and someone hairless has no hair to raise

explanation.surface: Acting rashly is hardly frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: To go at something bald-headed is a dated idiom for charging in without caution.
